headline: Approved new rules of procedure and postponed a $99.14 reimbursement for a climate conference.
summary: Engineers and city staff described the FEMA-funded back shore project on Long Point Road and Seashore Avenue, and residents asked many questions. The council also created a nominating committee and merged two committees into one called Sustainability.
decisions: Approved the September 23rd meeting minutes, unanimously.
Approved the October 7th meeting minutes, with Burton abstaining.
Approved creating a nominating committee for PIC members and a Maine Island Coalition alternate member, unanimously.
Approved adopting new rules of procedure and scrapping the PIC by-laws, publication schedule and work schedule, unanimously.
Approved combining the Environment & Sustainability committee with the Parks & Recreation committee into one committee named Sustainability, unanimously.
Postponed the $99.14 reimbursement for the October 17 Climate Resilience Conference to next month’s agenda, unanimously.

PIC October 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes, DRAFT. Page 1
             Peaks Island Council
             MEETING MINUTES
             Wednesday, October 28, 2026, 6:15 p.m.
              Hybrid ZOOM/in-person meeting in the Community Center
NEXT Regular Monthly PIC Meeting
    November 18, 2026
CALL TO ORDER: 6:15 p.m.
ROLL CALL
Present: Laura Glendening, Karsten Rees (remote), Jess Burton, Jonah Bradenday, Norm Proulx
Absent: Jerzy Sylvester
Number of Audience Members (AM) in attendance: 52 in person, 0 people attending remotely.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
Rees made motion to accept minutes from the September 23rd meeting. Proulx seconded. Unanimous 
approval. 
Rees made motion to accept minutes from the October 7th meeting. Bradenday seconded. Burton 
abstained. Other councilors gave approval. 
TREASURER’S REPORT 
Kate O’Sullivan said the only transaction was the purchase of 35 bicycle tickets. Rees asked O’Sullivan
Rees moved to accept the Treasurer’s Report. Bradenday seconded. Unanimous approval. 
ANNOUNCEMENTS
Rees encouraged people to subscribe to the newsletter and to consider joining the council.
Next PIC meeting is Wednesday, November 18th, at 6:15pm in the Community Center and on Google Meets.
Rees made a motion to go out of order to consider motion to create nominating committee first, then 
consider the motion to reconsider the presentation from the Public Works Department regarding FEMA 
funded project on the back shore and then revert back to original agenda. Bradenday seconded. 
Unanimous approval. 
 Motion to Create Nominating Committee for PIC Members and MIC Alternate 
Member. (KR) 
Rees made motion to create a nominating committee for PIC members and to nominate a Maine Island 
Coalition alternate member. Proulx seconded. 
Proulx asked if members of the committee have to be on the council. Rees said yes, they did. 
Ellen Mahoney explained that the Maine Islands Coalition meets quarterly and its goal is to have a voice at the 
state, local and federal level to advocate for sustainability on year-round islands, specifically transportation, 
housing, education, fisheries Mahoney is co-chair of MIC and asked if there was an islander who would be 
interested in joining the MIC. If people are interested and have questions, they should contact Ellen.
PIC October 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes, DRAFT. Page 2
No public comment. Rees said that Sylvester is willing to serve on the nominating committee. Burton will also 
serve on the nominating committee. Motion passed unanimously. 
 Motion to reconsider presentation from Department of Public Works 
regarding back shore. (KR)  
Rees made a motion to reconsider presentation from Department of Public Works regarding 
back shore. Bradenday seconded. 
Rees said the engineering staff will provide additional detail and then the public will be able to ask 
questions. 
Public comment:
AM asked if public will be able to ask questions of the engineering staff. 
AM asked if intent is to inform or to solicit public input. 
AM asked if engineering team could say what their instructions were when they were hired. 
Motion passed unanimously.
Keith Gray introduced engineering team (Leyna Tobey and Bill Walsh) and City Project manager (Kris 
DeVolder).
Kris DeVolder said the city is creating a website page that will go live tomorrow for more information. 
Leyna Tobey explained the process for this project. She said the two January 2024 storms were declared a 
disaster in March 2024. FEMA looked specifically at Long Point Road and Seashore Avenue. They itemize 
damages and spell out what they will and won’t pay for. Then FEMA allocated funding from two buckets, repair 
(pre-storm restoration) and mitigation (improvements). FEMA allocated $6 million to the project. FEMA will pay 
75%, the state will pay 15%, the city will pay 10%. In late 2025, the city selected Walsh Engineering to design 
the solution. 
AM asked about the requirements for public participation in the FEMA process. Tobey said there are no 
requirements for public participation, but the team will give the public an opportunity to participate. 
Gray said the intent of the funding is to repair the damage to pre-storm conditions and do some mitigation. 
AM asked if public mitigation is to preserve the road, protect the shoreline, maintain the views, or protect 
private property. Are the public dollars being used for public purposes or private purposes?
Tobey said that FEMA money must be spent solely on public protection. Private property protection is not a 
goal of the project. FEMA said that mitigation work could improve on the existing design of a riprap seawall 
that was lost during the storms. So, the design rebuilds the riprap wall and increases the height to increase 
resiliency. 
AM said that FEMA has dictated solutions according to their guidelines. but the community needs to have a 
conversation about what restrictions will be accepted along with the FEMA money.
PIC October 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes, DRAFT. Page 3
Gray said the engineering team and the public works department are trying to protect the road on the island, 
but there may have to be a compromise between resiliency and aesthetics if the community does not want the 
revetment wall. 
Tobey clarified that only one-quarter of Seashore Avenue will have revetement, with just one 250-foot section 
that is six feet high. 
AM asked if there has been any discussion about water flooding the marshes across the road. They also 
asked about visualizations of the project.
Tobey said that Walsh Engineering is sizing the culverts near the marshes to facilitate storm water drainage.
Rees said the existing information that includes some visualizations will be communicated to the public on the 
city website or via PIC communication. Gray said more visualizations will be created and made available on 
the city website.
Burton asked about when the work needs to be done in order to access the FEMA funding. Tobey said the 
money must be spent by December 31, 2027. Gray said the project is already behind and has already gotten 
an extension. The project needs to go out to bid as soon as possible although there is a little time to look at the 
plans and adjust them in the next few weeks. 
AM asked if any research has been done about what types of carcinogens or pollutants are in the marshes, 
one of which was a dump. Tobey said it was outside the scope of this project. Rees said that the community 
might want to include items that are just outside the scope of the project since this is closely related to the 
infrastructure items that are being reviewed.
AM asked if city council has oversight of this project. Councilor Machniewicz said the city council has no 
oversight of this project. Rees said that the process the city has designed over the next 30 days to increase 
communication with the public and to solicit public input. 
AM asked if there would be vegetation between the road and the riprap. AM also asked for public access to the 
beach at Spar Cove could be preserved over the riprap. Tobey said they are keeping a road shoulder that will 
be 2-3 feet. A staircase up and over the riprap at Spar Cove is also possible. 
AM asked how to find the city website with information about this project. DeVolder said the webpage will be 
on the city website. He will send a link to Karsten. 
AM asked Walsh Engineering to make drawings of the various sections so that islanders can visualize what 
the wall will look like. AM also said that preservation of the views on the back shore also benefits the city of 
Portland, not just Peaks island. The view is a resource that should be preserved.
AM said that the process seemed to have been going for a long time without input from the public. Can the 
project get another extension so that the public has a year to provide input? Gray said it is not too late to get 
public input but going back to the drawing board won’t result in anything new because the directive was to put 
back the pre-storm existing structures with some tweaks for improved resiliency. DeVolder said the limits of the 
time that can be requested from FEMA would be an extension to March 2028.
AM asked if the engineering team had considered a breakwater rather than a wall at the road. Tobey said 
breakwaters are much more expensive than the current budget and getting a permit would be difficult. Gray 
said it is not in the scope of work because it was not pre-existing. 
Glendening asked if public will be able to see all the questions on the website. DeVolder said yes.
AM asked if there is a final approval deadline for the project. Gray said the project should be finalized within 
the next few month or two. If no consensus is reached or the proposal is too far from the FEMA prescribed 
solution, then funding may have to be forfeited.
PIC October 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes, DRAFT. Page 4
Rees thanked the engineering team and the city public works department for their presentation.
PUBLIC COMMENT (public works related)
AM said that large trucks parked on the sides of the roads are making it difficult for traffic to pass and it’s 
difficult for people walking. Rees said that he will pass that comment on to Safety Committee Chair Sylvester.
AM said that the FEMA process has been going on for a year and a half and to be surprised at this point may 
be because individuals are not paying attention.
AM said that if PIC is going to vote on the project, they should vote on it by section, not as a whole. AM also 
said the report says the rocks at Long Point are not big enough and the report continues to say there will be no  
improvement, so the action contradicts the recommendation of the report.
AM asked the council to consider its communication of public works discussion so that there is 30-day notice of 
public works items. 
COMMITTEE REPORTS & UPDATES 
 Executive Committee 
Rees said that the city council voted on the PIC recommendation that city council amend their procedural 
rules in regard to PIC putting items on the city council agenda, and in regard to the city council referring 
island-specific items to PIC. 
The city council voted in favor of referring more items to PIC, and they committed to think more about PIC 
when they make their plans. 
The city council was not comfortable with the mechanism that PIC proposed for putting items on the city 
council agenda. Councilor Grant asked to continue the conversation to address the objective of the PIC 
recommendation. Rees will discuss with Councilor Grant.
 Environment and Sustainability 
Glendening said she spoke with Katie Hagar at City Emergency Planning She will be presenting on 
emergency operations plan in April. Hagar said there is no evacuation plan for Peaks Island. The Island 
Institute is going to help work on some evacuation plans for Peaks Island. 
Bradenday said he reached out to Kate Snyder and Joey Brunelle (running for city council at-large position) 
about installing a bathroom at the ballpark. They both said they were on board with installing a bathroom at 
the ballpark. 
Rees said that Parks and Recreation and Waterfront should lead the work on the issue of removing the boat 
cradles left on Ferry Beach. Rees will reach out to the owner of the boat cradles to ask them about removing 
them from public property. AM asked why the city is not reaching out to the owner. Rees said it falls within 
the purview of the Peaks Island Council and the issue can be escalated if no action is taken.
 Ferry Services and Access 
Rees said that PITEA submitted a report about last month’s expenditures for needs-based tickets and 
passes. They have spent about $2,000-$3,000. Burton commented that the reports are great and Michele 
Winchester is very responsive to questions.
Rees said that the PUC is continuing its regulatory review of passenger ticket price increase.
PIC October 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes, DRAFT. Page 5
 Housing and Zoning Committee
Rees said there were conversations about how the committee can collaborate with Home Start. A housing 
needs survey is being considered to identify Peaks Island housing needs.
• Parking
No updates.
 Paper Roads 
No update.
 Parks, Recreation and Waterfront Committee
The committee met with the Environment and Sustainability committee.
 Safety Committee 
No update. 
UNFINISHED BUSINESS – 
● Motion to Adopt Rules of Procedure (KR)
Rees said that the motion has already been made and seconded. Rees said the council reviewed the 
Rules of Procedure at a special meeting held on October 7th. 
The document is available here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wWHb9_BJzercxpUWVzPVN0CwL_OAg1CHCxOVCnQk4MU/e
dit?tab=t.0 
Rees reviewed minor edits.
1) Part 1 -  Insert language to say that PIC complies with state, local and federal law.
2) Rule 10b - Specify the agenda for the Inaugural Meeting.
3) Rule 10c, part iv - Specify that officers must be approved by four PIC members.
4) Rule 13a - Specify that the island liaison gets a copy of the PIC meeting agendas.
5) Rule 13c - Rees said they need to get input from Sarah Michniewicz about the best way to inform city 
council about PIC minutes and agenda.
6) Rule 14a, part iv – Specify that vice chair transmits budget to city manager.
7) Rule 15a - Specify PIC process is democratic and based on consensus.
8) Rule 21b - PIC councilors serve until their successors are sworn in. 
9) Rule 22 – Specify procedure for appointing Peaks Island representative to Maine Island Coalition 
10) Appendix B – written templates and examples for PIC orders and resolutions
Glendening stated that there should be a mechanism for members of the public to request a presentation to 
the PIC. Rees said that is covered in Rule 2c, Introduction of Business. 
Glendening asked if committee structure should be updated. Rees said that could be adjusted in December 
after new committee structure is voted on.
AM asked if agenda items could be posted in writing on bulletin boards. Rees said there is not administrative 
capacity to do that, but members of the public could do it if they wanted to. Glendening said that PIC can think 
about how to handle that before the December meeting. Rees said the PIC rules state the meeting agenda is 
set five days in advance.
PIC October 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes, DRAFT. Page 6
Rees restated the motion on the table is for PIC to adopt the new rules of procedure and scrap the PIC 
By-laws, publication schedule and work schedule. Motion passed unanimously. 
NEW BUSINESS
● Motion to combine Environment & Sustainability with Parks & Rec, and to 
nominate Jonah to chair the Parking Committee. (LG)
Glendening made a motion to combine the Environment & Sustainability committee with the 
Parks & Recreation committee and to rename the new committee to Sustainability. Bradenday 
seconded. 
Rees asked if the name of the committee should be Sustainability. Councilors decided it would be fine 
to be broad at this time.
Motion passed unanimously. 
● Motion for the PIC to contribute $99.14 to the cost of the October 17 Climate 
Resilience Conference. (LG)
Glendening said a community member asked to be reimbursed for expenditures for the island’s 
Climate Resilience Conference.
Glendening made a motion to reimburse a receipt for expenditures for the island’s Climate 
Resilience Conference. Rees seconded.
Rees said that the current budget may not have $99 for the reimbursement. If the community member 
could wait until the next fiscal budget in eight months, they could be reimbursed then. Burton 
suggested moving the item to next month’s agenda when councilors will know if there is money in the 
budget. Rees said PIC is authorized to fundraise and can get non-municipal funding for projects. 
Glendening said future budgets
Rees moved to postpone further discussion of agenda item to next month’s agenda. 
Glendening seconded. Motion to postpone passed unanimously. 
● Report out on the Climate Conference. (Jess B.)
Burton said the conference was well attended. Excellent presentations in the morning, a Q&A panel, 
lunch with a Peaks Island Compost Project presentation. In the afternoon presentations about ways 
islanders can get involved with climate resiliency on Peaks Island including lawn care, Peaks Island 
CERT emergency response team, energy efficiency, shoreline erosion, Burton is going to request the 
notes from the conference and post them on the PIC drive.
ADDITIONAL PUBLIC COMMENT
AM asked PIC to resurrect the golf cart parking plan for the sidewalk across from Peaks Island Lobster 
Company. Rees asked AM to deliver plans to Bradenday. 
Rees made a motion to adjourn. Bradenday seconded. Motion passed unanimously.
Meeting Adjournment:   8:59 p.m.
